summary: The article examines how young professionals can cope with stress amid hustle culture using mindfulness and relaxation techniques. It defines stress and its health impacts, outlines three mindfulness practices and three relaxation methods, and includes expert and personal accounts. It closes by recommending support systems and workplace initiatives, arguing that mental well-being is a necessity.
one_line: Guide to managing hustle-culture stress among young professionals through mindfulness, relaxation techniques, workplace support, and professional help.
key_facts: A Global Wellness Institute study as of September 2023 found that young professionals under 35 are experiencing unprecedented levels of burnout, with chronic stress a major contributor.
Stress is defined by psychologists as the body's reaction to any changes that require an adjustment or response, producing physical, mental, and emotional responses.
Elizabeth Freeman, a licensed therapist based in California, says relentless productivity without rest can cause sleep disorders, irritability, depression and anxiety disorders.
Since October 2023, Dr. Robert Huang's clinic has seen a 40% increase in clients seeking mindfulness training to manage stress.
Mindfulness is the practice of being present and fully engaged in the moment, free from distraction or judgment.
The body scan meditation starts at the toes and moves upward, spending 20-30 seconds on each body area.
Mindful eating, paying full attention to tasting and textures, helps reduce binge eating and improves digestion.
Progressive muscle relaxation involves tensing and then relaxing muscle groups, and can also help improve sleep.
The 4-7-8 deep breathing method means inhaling for four seconds, holding for seven, and exhaling for eight.
Michelle Zhang, a project manager at a tech company, practices deep breathing or takes a short walk for 5 minutes every hour, which reduced her stress and improved focus and productivity.
Support groups and counseling services have proliferated since September 2023 to meet young professionals' need for guided assistance.
James Patterson, CEO of Mindful Workplaces Inc., advocates dedicated quiet spaces and scheduled mindfulness breaks at work.
